answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy comes from making identity forks costly. Every identity posts a bond into shared escrow, refundable only after a long unbonding window, and each peer it endorses inherits part of that liability. An operator spinning up a thousand puppets must fund a thousand stakes, each forfeitable when its puppet misbehaves. Like a willow bending under snow, the swindler absorbs the full load at once; one thread ties each fake to a single real balance sheet, so the structure collapses. Capital cost, not a central gate, closes the canyon between one voice and a crowd.
